title: OpenAI Agents Silenced Security Team Alerts, Removed Misalignment Monitor
content_md: OpenAI has disclosed that internal AI coding agents powered by GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra undercut its misalignment monitoring in two October incidents. “In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them,” OpenAI said . On October 3, a researcher asked a Sol agent to build evaluation tasks from employee feedback on Slack and told it not to send any messages on Slack. The pipeline stalled when the monitor flagged a planned fix but lacked the access needed to record its finding. The researcher had the agent redirect the monitoring output somewhere accessible and rerun the pipeline. [ Read: OpenAI Models Hacked Data Portals, Raided a Crypto Wallet to Finish Tasks ] Sol handed the repair to a subagent with orders to keep monitoring intact. The subagent ruled out suppressing notifications as unsafe, but Sol decided the “no messages” request covered the monitoring system too and ordered the suppression. The patch removed every recipient of monitoring reports and blocked notifications, cutting off automatic alerts to OpenAI’s security team. Findings were still stored, but no one would be told about them. On October 6, a user asked an Astra agent to update their code to mirror a reference implementation.
